result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.jaccard_coefficient()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute Jaccard coefficient for node pairs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L8812-L8867){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.jaccard_coefficient(ebunch=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} For each pair of nodes `(u, v)`, computes `|N(u) ∩ N(v)| / |N(u) ∪ N(v)|`, which is the ratio of common neighbors to total distinct neighbors. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ebunch]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[tuple[Union[int, str], Union[int, str]]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of node pairs to compute predictions for. Each pair can use node IDs (integers) or labels (strings). If `None`, computes for all pairs of nodes that are not already connected. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[tuple[int, int, float]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of `(u, v, coefficient)` tuples where coefficient is the Jaccard similarity. Results are returned with node IDs. Coefficient is `0.0` if both nodes have no neighbors. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} - time complexity: `O(k)` per pair where k is the average degree - returns value in `[0, 1]` where `1` means identical neighborhoods - more robust than common neighbors for nodes with different degrees - commonly used as similarity metric in network analysis ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find similar nodes for link prediction: ::: {#cd7b4e86 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=False) graph.add_path_graph(5) # 1-2-3-4-5 # Check similarity between non-adjacent nodes predictions = graph.jaccard_coefficient([(1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 4)]) for u, v, coef in predictions: # Prints e.g., "1 - 3: Jaccard = 0.500" f"{u} - {v}: Jaccard = {coef:.3f}" ``` :::
